title: Demographics Are Destiny For Cannabis And I’m Old and Grumpy, So Listen Up!

content_html_sanitized:
Both Yogi Berra, the baseball player and Niels Bohr, the physicist, are credited with the quip that it’s difficult to make predictions, especially about the future. So it must be true.

However, there’s one exception to that rule, demographics.

In all of the developed countries the birth rates are far below the needed 2.1 children per female needed just to keep the population from falling. The mathematically inevitable consequence of that fact is that the average age of the population of these countries is getting older. (Immigration is a partial solution, but that obviously has its problems.)

Also, as the population ages, the need for medical care is increasing, but doctors are also aging rapidly, and retiring, so the cost of medical care is increasing. Supply and demand. But even in the richest countries, money alone cannot solve this problem.

Artificial intelligence will aid in diagnosing symptoms, and a greater reliance on “nursing” will help, but most of the people are “just getting old”, and surviving the occasional infirmities associated therewith.

Unfortunately, the pharmaceuticals that are commonly prescribed in advanced countries can be addictive, dangerous in the short run, and  even deadly in the longer term.

See Nocturnal benzodiazepines have a significant negative health impact on the elderly, yet they continue to be used.

And A systematic review of opioid and benzodiazepine misuse in older adults


By the way, benzodiazepines are one of the only two addictive drugs that withdrawal from which can be fatal. The other is alcohol. The Dangers of Benzo Detox and Xanax Withdrawal


And it is a global problem.

See “Estimates of the number of benzodiazepine-dependent persons in Germany range from 128 000 to 1.6 million”


Of course, just getting access to prescription drugs can be challenging for the elderly, requiring a trip to the doctor’s office and then to the pharmacy.


Then there is medical cannabis. What an easy solution! Well, maybe not.


First, the politicians have to change the laws, which they are very slow about doing. Eleven states still have not passed any medical marijuana laws, and some of them are extremely cumbersome.


And then there is the absurdity of giving the medical profession control over access to cannabis after they have been opposing it for decades.


Ironically, the absurd federal Drug Scheduling has avoided that problem in the US, up until now, but that could change if cannabis is simply rescheduled, as is now being discussed.

See DEA FINALLY CONFIRMS THE EXISTENCE OF SUFFICIENT GROUNDS TO REMOVE MARIJUANA FROM HARD DRUGS SCHEDULE OF CONTROLLED SUBSTANCES


Oops! Terribly sorry. That is actually from 1998. 


Here is a more recent report.

DEA gives cannabis rescheduling update (Newsletter: April 11, 2025)


As they say at the DEA, you should live so long. Twenty seven years is no time at all, as long as you’re not in pain and you’re not in prison.


Which brings me back to talkin’ ‘bout my gggeneration. 


As the population ages, and more and more voters recognize that medical cannabis can help them with the unavoidable problems of aging, the pressure on our politicians will inevitably bring about real change.


But in the meantime, disabled veterans still can’t get cannabis at Veterans Administration hospitals. Thanks for your service???

See Marijuana in Veterans’ Medical Treatment Medical cannabis as an alternative to opioids for veterans 

Obviously, I don’t have any difficulty getting access to medical cannabis, but it’s really outrageous that the marijuana reform movement has a more compassionate veterans program than the United States military.
